hero.title: Counselling and clinical supervision, without the runaround.
hero.lead: I'm John Goss. Practising since 2015, seeing people one to one, as couples, and as a supervisor to other therapists. In person in Bletchley, Milton Keynes, or online anywhere in the UK.
hero.reassure: Phone, email or [WhatsApp](https://wa.me/447776153426) me directly. There is no booking form and no online calendar.

steps.heading: What happens when you get in touch
steps.intro: Nothing is hidden behind an enquiry. Fees are on this page, in full, including the lower-fee appointments I can sometimes offer if you're on a low income.

items.title: You ring, email or WhatsApp
items.body: Whichever suits you: the number, the address and the WhatsApp link are on this page, and they are the only way in. Nothing to fill in first.

items.title: We talk about what's going on
items.body: A short conversation about what you're looking for, what I do, and whether I'm the right person for it. There's no charge for that and no obligation either way.

items.title: We agree a time and a fee
items.body: Sessions are 50 or 90 minutes, in person in MK3 or online. We settle the fee from the published range before we start, so nothing is a surprise.

services.heading: How I can help
services.intro: Therapy, and your reasons for thinking about coming to see me, will be unique to you. These are the four ways I usually work.

items.title: Individual counselling
items.body:
We meet one to one to explore what's challenging you. For some people that's anxiety, depression or bereavement. You might be looking to explore your relationship with pornography or sex.

Whatever brings you to counselling, you are assured of a space to talk openly about it.

items.title: Relationship counselling
items.body: Relationship counselling puts the focus on the relationship itself, whatever shape it takes. You won't need to explain or justify that shape to me before we start.

items.title: Psychosexual therapy
items.body:
If you're experiencing sexual difficulties, psychosexual therapy could be for you: pain during sex, unreliable erections, delayed ejaculation, low or absent desire, vaginismus, orgasm difficulties, vulvodynia.

People also come to talk about porn use, intimacy with a partner or partners, fetishes, or exploring kink.

items.title: Clinical supervision
items.body:
I offer clinical supervision to other therapists and to colleagues working in the helping professions.

Supervision isn't only about bringing your client work; it's about bringing yourself too, so we can explore that work more collaboratively.

I hold a Level 6 Diploma in Clinical Supervision (2022) and I'm an NCPS Accredited Member, so the hours count towards your professional requirements. If you work with sexual behaviour, harmful sexual behaviour or risk, that is territory I have specific training in; see the qualifications below.

about.heading: About me
about.body:
Thanks for visiting. I qualified as a counsellor in 2015, after a range of experience in support work: youth mentoring, Samaritans, and supporting people in prison.

I see myself very much as an *integrative* therapist: I use all of my training to support you, rather than sticking to a single theory. Some people come to me for something specific, such as a sexual difficulty, but the rest of my skills and training are in the room too.

My counselling work is varied, often with anxiety, depression and bereavement. I'm also training further as a psychosexual therapist, working with painful sex, unreliable erections and other sex-related concerns.

fees.heading: What sessions cost
fees.intro: In person in MK3, or online. Fees are given as a range and we agree yours before we start.

note.title: If you're on a low income
note.body: To keep counselling accessible, I'm sometimes able to offer appointments at a lower fee. [Get in touch](mailto:info@gosscounselling.co.uk) to find out more; it's a normal thing to ask.

items.q: How many sessions will I need?
items.a: There isn't necessarily a set amount of therapy you 'need'; it depends on what you're coming for and what you'd like from the sessions. We can discuss it when we start, and keep it under review.

items.q: What sort of therapy do you offer?
items.a: I see myself very much as an integrative therapist: I use all my training to support you, without sticking to one type of theory. Some people come for something specific, like a sexual issue, which would fit under psychosexual therapy, but I'd still be using all my other skills and training too.

Psychosexual therapy generally focuses on a sexual issue. That could include:

- Unreliable erections
- Delayed ejaculation
- Loss of, or lack of, sexual desire
- Vaginismus
- Painful sex
- Orgasm problems
- Vulvodynia

People also see a psychosexual therapist for other reasons: porn use, intimacy with a partner or partners, fetishes, or exploring kinks.

items.q: Is there a difference between counselling, therapy and psychotherapy?
items.a: The simple answer is no. In the UK, terms such as counsellor, therapist and psychotherapist aren't protected by law, so people use them interchangeably. I usually use 'counsellor' or 'therapist'. Some membership bodies and some therapists do differentiate, but in UK law there's no distinction.

As a therapist I'm self-employed, so there's no sick pay or employee benefits. There's also the training and qualifications to pay for, and continuing professional development that never stops.

The session fee has to take account of my qualifications and what they cost, along with practical things like room hire and Zoom licences.
